sanity_expectations: v is finite, real, and non-negative for all sampled S > 0
v increases roughly linearly at S << Km (v ≈ Vmax*S/Km)
v attains a single maximum at S* = sqrt(Km*Ksi) ≈ 10 with v_peak ≈ 0.833
v decreases toward 0 for S >> sqrt(Km*Ksi) (substrate inhibition regime)
Curve is unimodal in log(S) with no oscillation
excitation_report: Full RHS (single top-level term as an explicit rational expression) reaches ~24.6*sigma over the sampled log-range S in [0.01, 1000]. Peak of v ≈ 0.833 at S = sqrt(Km*Ksi) = 10; rise (S<<Km), peak, and inhibition regime (S>>sqrt(Km*Ksi)) are all captured. sigma=0.02 is ~2.4% of the peak.
role_corrections: v: O->O (confirmed dependent variable, LHS of explicit relation)
S: 'input/time axis' -> V (confirmed as the sole independent axis to sample; substrate concentration)
Vmax: 'input/time axis' -> P (overridden: fixed kinetic parameter, not sampled)
Km: 'input/time axis' -> P (overridden: fixed half-saturation constant, not sampled)
Ksi: 'input/time axis' -> P (overridden: fixed inhibition constant, not sampled)
rationale: Structure (analyze_expression) confirms an explicit algebraic relation solvable for v with free symbols {S, Vmax, Km, Ksi} and no derivatives/integrals. Only S is a natural sampling axis; Vmax/Km/Ksi are fixed physical constants of the enzyme, hence parameters. Values chosen so that substrate inhibition is expressed within a physically reasonable range: Km=1 sets the low-S half-saturation, Ksi=100 (>> Km) sets a well-separated inhibition scale, yielding a peak at S*=sqrt(Km*Ksi)=10, with v_peak=Vmax/(1+2*sqrt(Km/Ksi))≈0.833. Log-spaced sampling of S in [0.01, 1000] over 300 points covers the linear-rise, saturation, peak, and inhibition-driven decline regimes.
